connection: Session 21 returned deferred Where/OrderBy pipelines, and Sum enumerated its input to calculate one number. Session 22 deliberately called ToList to run a report query and save a snapshot. Session 23 isolates that timing distinction in permanent xUnit tests.
objectives: Distinguish creating a deferred Where query from enumerating it.
Prove that a deferred query observes source changes made before enumeration.
Use ToList when a fixed snapshot is required immediately.
Explain how xUnit compares sequences with different concrete container types.
Recognize IQueryable as a later provider-based variation without memorizing it now.

visuals.title: Where defines work that can run later
visuals.explanation: IEnumerable<ClockEntry> is something that can be enumerated to produce values. Calling Where may build a deferred pipeline; it is not a JavaScript Promise or a C# Task.

visuals.title: Enumeration runs the deferred pipeline
visuals.explanation: foreach, Assert.Equal's sequence comparison, Sum, and ToList must request elements. That enumeration is where the deferred Where work runs.

visuals.title: ToList runs now and saves a snapshot
visuals.explanation: ToList enumerates immediately and stores the current matching elements in a new List. Later changes to the source do not alter that snapshot.

visuals.title: IQueryable defers to a provider, not just to enumeration
visuals.explanation: Later EF Core IQueryable queries may defer provider-translated work such as SQL. The shared idea is deferred execution; the execution mechanism and location differ.

preQuiz.prompt: When does GetEmployeeClockEntries's Where clause actually run?
options: When the returned IEnumerable<ClockEntry> is enumerated (a foreach, ToList, or Sum) -- not when GetEmployeeClockEntries itself is called
Immediately, inside the GetEmployeeClockEntries call
Never -- Where is evaluated at compile time
preQuiz.explanation: IEnumerable's Where is deferred: calling GetEmployeeClockEntries builds a query description, and CalculateTotalHours's .Sum() is what actually walks _clockEntries and applies the filter.

preQuiz.prompt: If a new ClockEntry is added to _clockEntries after GetEmployeeClockEntries returns but before .Sum() enumerates it, what happens?
options: The new entry can be included in the sum, since the query re-reads the live list at enumeration time
The new entry is guaranteed to be excluded
An exception is thrown
preQuiz.explanation: Deferred execution means the query is a live view over _clockEntries at the moment it is enumerated, not a snapshot taken when GetEmployeeClockEntries was called.

preQuiz.prompt: What does .ToList() do differently from just holding an IEnumerable<ClockEntry> reference?
options: It forces immediate enumeration and copies matching elements into a new List, fixed at that moment
It changes the Where clause's filtering logic
It converts the query into an IQueryable
preQuiz.explanation: ToList materializes: it runs the deferred query right now and returns a stable snapshot that later changes to the source will not affect.

concept.title: Where defines a deferred query
paragraphs: IEnumerable<T> is something that can be enumerated to produce values. Calling it a promise can be a useful analogy, but it is not a JavaScript Promise and it is not a C# Task.

Calling Where returns a new sequence and does not modify source. For reference types it normally yields references to the same objects rather than cloning them. Memory anchor from Session 21: New sequence. Same objects.

Creating evens does not copy 1 and 2. The Where pipeline retains source as its input and reads that source when enumeration begins. A LINQ result must be stored, returned, or enumerated; discarding it accomplishes nothing useful.

concept.title: Assert.Equal enumerates the deferred sequence
paragraphs: new[] { 2, 4 } is an int array, while evens is an IEnumerable<int>. They are different concrete types, but both represent sequences of integers.

xUnit's sequence-aware Assert.Equal compares their elements in order. To compare the contents, it enumerates evens; that enumeration triggers the deferred Where query after source.Add(4). Memory anchor: Different containers. Same element sequence.

This is sequence equality, not reference equality. Reference equality asks whether two variables refer to the same object; sequence equality asks whether enumeration produces equal elements in the same order.
concept.code:
source.Add(4);
Assert.Equal(new[] { 2, 4 }, evens); // Enumerates evens here.

concept.title: ToList runs immediately and stores current results
paragraphs: ToList enumerates the Where query immediately and stores its current elements in a new List<int>. Changing source afterward does not update snapshot.
Use source.Add(4) to test snapshot isolation. Calling snapshot.Add(4) would mutate the snapshot itself and would not prove anything about whether source changes affect it.
List<T> implements IEnumerable<T>, so more LINQ can still follow ToList. The distinction is timing: No ToList: run later. ToList: run now and save the results.

concept.title: Why permanent tests instead of ScratchPad
paragraphs: ScratchPad is for exploring syntax and observing behavior. Unit tests preserve behavioral claims that must remain true as the code changes. Memory anchor: Explore in ScratchPad. Protect behavior with tests.

Earlier ScratchPad experiments remain valuable and are not replaced. A later optional reinforcement lab could convert selected production rules—such as rejecting a second clock-in—into permanent tests after the testing foundation is established; this audit proposes that idea but does not add the lab.
concept.code:
// This assertion permanently protects the timing claim.
Assert.Equal(new[] { 2, 4 }, evens);

concept.title: Repeated enumeration reruns deferred work
paragraphs: Enumerating the same deferred query twice over an in-memory List runs the filtering work twice, and source changes may affect the later result.
Session 21's Sum enumerates because it must inspect the input to produce one final number. Session 22's ToList deliberately enumerates once and saves its completed report snapshot.
Later, repeatedly enumerating an IQueryable database query may issue repeated database queries. Sessions 31–32 cover provider translation and SQL; for now, retain only that preview.
concept.code:
int count = evens.Count(); // first enumeration
int total = evens.Sum();  // second enumeration

lab.objective: Correct and complete two permanent xUnit tests that prove when Where runs and when ToList saves a snapshot.
lab.startingCondition: The actual Domain.Tests project already contains xUnit 2.9.3, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 17.14.1, xunit.runner.visualstudio 3.1.4, implicit usings, and a global Xunit using. UnitTest1.cs is already absent. DeferredExecutionTests.cs exists with meaningful in-progress tests, so preserve it and correct it rather than deleting or replacing it.
steps: Open tests/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Domain.Tests/DeferredExecutionTests.cs; preserve the existing DeferredExecutionTests class and both in-progress Fact methods.

Remove using System.Diagnostics.Tracing from DeferredExecutionTests.cs because this test file does not use that namespace. Do not add using Xunit because the test project already supplies a global Xunit using.
In DeferredExecutionTests.DeferredQuery_SeesValuesAddedBeforeEnumeration, change List<int> source so it initially contains 1 and 2.

In DeferredQuery_SeesValuesAddedBeforeEnumeration, keep IEnumerable<int> evens assigned from source.Where(value => value % 2 == 0). Remember: Where returns a new deferred sequence and does not modify source.
Do not enumerate evens immediately after creating it.
In DeferredQuery_SeesValuesAddedBeforeEnumeration, call source.Add(4) after evens has been defined.
In DeferredQuery_SeesValuesAddedBeforeEnumeration, change Assert.Equal so its actual argument is evens rather than source.
Immediately above the first Assert.Equal, add a comment stating that Assert.Equal enumerates evens and therefore runs Where at that line.
Remember for the first assertion: new[] { 2, 4 } is an int array and evens is IEnumerable<int>, but xUnit compares the integer elements in order. Different containers. Same element sequence.
Rename the second Fact method from DefferedExecutionsTests to MaterializedQuery_DoesNotChangeWithSource.
In MaterializedQuery_DoesNotChangeWithSource, create a separate List<int> source containing 1 and 2.
Remove the unused evens variable from MaterializedQuery_DoesNotChangeWithSource.
In MaterializedQuery_DoesNotChangeWithSource, call Where on source to keep even numbers, immediately call ToList, and store the resulting List<int> in snapshot.
In MaterializedQuery_DoesNotChangeWithSource, call source.Add(4) after snapshot has been created; do not call snapshot.Add(4), because the test is proving isolation from changes to source.
In MaterializedQuery_DoesNotChangeWithSource, assert that snapshot contains only 2.
Immediately above the second Assert.Equal, add a comment stating that ToList already ran the query and saved its results before source changed.

steps.text: Run the focused DeferredExecutionTests, then build and test the complete solution. Open the Solution Reveal only after both tests pass.

dotnet test tests/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Domain.Tests/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Domain.Tests.csproj --configuration Release --filter FullyQualifiedName~DeferredExecutionTests

dotnet test PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release --no-build

reveals.title: Solution
reveals.text: The first assertion enumerates evens after source changes. The second assertion reads a List snapshot created before its separate source changes.

lab.expectedBehavior: The first test passes because Assert.Equal enumerates the deferred evens query after 4 is added to source. The second passes because ToList saved a List<int> snapshot before its separate source received 4.
lab.validation: dotnet build PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release && dotnet test PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release --no-build

postQuiz.prompt: In DeferredQuery_SeesValuesAddedBeforeEnumeration, which line first enumerates evens?
options: Assert.Equal(new[] { 2, 4 }, evens)
The Where assignment
source.Add(4)
postQuiz.explanation: Assert.Equal must compare the sequence elements, so it enumerates evens and runs the deferred Where pipeline.

postQuiz.prompt: Why does source.Add(4) belong in the snapshot test instead of snapshot.Add(4)?
options: Changing source tests whether the already-materialized snapshot is isolated from later source changes
snapshot cannot store 4
source.Add automatically calls ToList again
postQuiz.explanation: Mutating snapshot would directly change the result being asserted and would not test materialization timing.

postQuiz.prompt: How can Assert.Equal compare an int[] with an IEnumerable<int>?
options: xUnit enumerates both and compares their integer elements in order
It converts both variables to the same object reference
Arrays and IEnumerable are the same concrete type
postQuiz.explanation: Different containers can represent the same element sequence; sequence-aware equality compares the produced elements in order.

postQuiz.prompt: What happens if the same deferred in-memory query is enumerated twice?
options: Its filtering work normally runs twice, and later source changes may affect the second result
The first result is automatically cached
The second enumeration cannot compile
postQuiz.explanation: Deferred IEnumerable queries normally run again for each enumeration. A later IQueryable may also cause another database query.

reflections: Predict both assertions before running the tests.
Identify the exact line where evens is first enumerated.
If source.Add(6) occurs before the first assertion, what sequence should xUnit observe?
What changes if ToList moves from the snapshot assignment to immediately before its assertion?
Why would snapshot.Add(4) test a different claim from source.Add(4)?
whatBreaks: Asserting against source instead of evens makes the first test pass without proving deferred Where execution. Keeping an unused evens variable in the snapshot test distracts from the one query whose timing matters. Calling snapshot.Add(4) mutates the saved result itself and does not test isolation from later source changes. Repeatedly enumerating deferred work reruns it and can observe new source state; later IQueryable repetition may also repeat database calls.
summary: Session 23 proves one distinction: Where defines a query that runs when enumerated, while ToList runs that query immediately and saves the current results. Assert.Equal performs the first test's enumeration and compares sequence elements even though the expected array and actual IEnumerable have different concrete types. Explore in ScratchPad; protect behavioral claims with tests.
